title: Legendre's Conjecture: Prime Between n² and (n+1)²

problemStatement.plain: Legendre's conjecture (1798) asserts there is always a prime between consecutive perfect squares. One of Landau's four problems; open. Verified computationally to n ≤ 1.5 × 10^18.
whyMatters: Landau problem (1912) — one of four 'unattackable' problems
Equivalent to prime gap bound g(p_k) ≤ 2√p_k + 1
Not implied by RH (RH gives only g ≪ √p log p, one log too weak)
Connection to Cramér heuristic on prime gaps

proven: Verified computationally for n ≤ 1.5 × 10^18 (Nicely et al.)
In this repo, legendre-partial verified n = 1, …, 20 via native_decide
Baker–Harman–Pintz (2001): primes in [x, x + x^0.525] — does not reach Legendre
knownResults.goal: Initial survey; identify tractable sub-milestone for iteration 2 (recommended: equivalence with prime-gap bound)

knowledge.progressSummary: Surveyed literature: full conjecture infeasible (not even implied by RH). Identified three sub-milestones: (A) Cramér ⇒ Legendre eventually, (B) equivalence with prime-gap bound, (C) computational extension. Recommend B for iteration 2.
insights: Legendre is NOT implied by RH — Cramér's RH-based bound g ≪ √p log p has an extra logarithmic factor relative to what Legendre needs
Bertrand's postulate is too weak by a factor of ~n: it gives a prime in (n², 2n²) but Legendre needs the prime in (n², (n+1)²) — an interval of length 2n+1, vs Bertrand's interval of length n²
Best unconditional short-interval result (Baker–Harman–Pintz 2001) is θ = 0.525, still missing Legendre's θ = 0.5
The conjecture is equivalent to the prime-gap bound g(p_k) ≤ 2√p_k + 1 for all k — this gives a clean reformulation suitable for Lean
Mathlib lacks a primeGap definition; introducing one would benefit other gallery proofs
mathlibGaps: No short-interval prime theorems (Hoheisel, Huxley, BHP)
No Legendre conjecture statement (only the partial version in legendre-partial)
nextSteps: Sub-Milestone B (recommended): formalize equivalence Legendre ↔ ∀k, p_(k+1) − p_k ≤ 2√p_k
Sub-Milestone A: formalize Cramér ⇒ Legendre eventually
Sub-Milestone C: extend native_decide verification to n ≤ 100 (low value)
